the following question: How can we compare the development performance and product of two different software processes, and how can we evaluate the effect of these processes on the performance and product?

The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to compare two development models by using a systematic method and quantitative analysis, and the comparison results can provide objective evidence for the adoption decision.

Agile software development models are more effective than the traditional software development models in terms of productivity, defect density, defect resolution effort ratio, test execution V&V effectiveness, and effort prediction capability.

it is feasible to use a systematic approach to compare the effectiveness of different software development processes in a real-world setting, and to use the results of such comparisons to drive process improvement.
